title: Provide alt text for images that carry information
statement: An image conveying content a reader needs - a chart, a diagram, a photograph of the product, a screenshot, an image used as a link or a button - has alt text that conveys the same information in words.
rationale: Alt text is the only representation of the image available to a reader using a screen reader, to a browser that failed to load it, and to anything indexing the page as text, so an informative image without it simply has no content.
implementation: Write the text from what the image communicates in its context, not from the filename or a keyword list. Where the image is the content of a link, describe the destination rather than the picture. An automated agent may report a missing value but must not invent a description of an image it cannot see.

verification.method: Collect every image element in the served response together with its alt attribute and role, and report informative images whose alt attribute is absent.

title: Mark decorative images with an empty alt attribute
statement: An image that adds no information a reader needs - a background texture, a spacer, a repeated ornament, an icon beside text that already says the same thing - carries an alt attribute present but empty rather than absent.
rationale: An absent attribute makes assistive technology fall back to announcing the file name, so the reader is read a URL instead of being allowed to skip an element that carried nothing.
implementation: Decide per image whether it informs or decorates, and set the empty attribute only for the decorative case. Where the image is purely presentational, moving it into CSS removes the question entirely.

verification.method: Report images whose alt attribute is absent, separating those that duplicate adjacent text or serve as ornament from those that carry content.

title: Declare intrinsic dimensions on rendered images
statement: Every image element declares width and height attributes matching the asset's intrinsic pixel dimensions, or a framework component that emits them on its behalf, so the space the image will occupy is known before it loads.
rationale: Without declared dimensions the browser cannot reserve space, so the content below the image moves once it arrives, and the reader loses their place through no action of their own.
implementation: Read the dimensions from the asset at build time rather than hand-writing them, and set the aspect ratio in CSS so a responsive width still reserves the right height. Do not copy the displayed size into the attributes when it differs from the file.

verification.method: Compare each declared width and height against the intrinsic dimensions of the fetched asset and report images with absent or mismatched values.

title: Serve responsive image candidates sized for the layout
statement: An image whose displayed width varies with the viewport offers several candidate sources with their pixel widths declared, together with a description of the space it will occupy, so the browser can choose rather than always fetching the largest file.
rationale: A single large asset scaled down in the browser transfers bytes no reader benefits from, and on a narrow connection those bytes delay the content the reader came for.
implementation: Generate the candidate set from the source asset during the build, or use the framework image component that does so, and describe the layout width honestly rather than copying a value from another template. A fixed-size image needs no candidate set.

verification.method: Load each page at several viewport widths and record which candidate the browser selected against the width the image actually occupied.

title: Exclude the largest visible image from lazy loading
statement: Images below the initial viewport defer their load, while the image most likely to be the largest element visible on arrival loads eagerly and is not deferred by a lazy-loading attribute or a script-based loader.
rationale: Deferring the image the reader is waiting for delays the moment the page appears finished, so applying the attribute uniformly across a template makes the most important image the slowest one.
implementation: Identify the hero or leading image per template and opt it out of the deferring attribute explicitly, rather than applying the attribute in a shared component with no exception. Verify per template, because which image leads differs between them.

verification.method: Measure which element is the largest painted in the viewport on load and confirm it is not among the images marked for deferred loading.

sources.title: Browser-level image lazy loading for the web

title: Keep discoverable images fetchable by image crawlers
statement: Images intended to be found are served from URLs that no crawl directive blocks, return a successful response without requiring a session, and are referenced from a page that is itself indexable.
rationale: An image blocked by a directive or gated behind a session cannot be fetched, so it is absent from image results regardless of how well the page around it is described.
implementation: Check the crawl directives against the asset paths, including any CDN or transformation host that serves them, and keep private media on a separate path that stays blocked. Do not remove a directive that protects genuinely private media in order to satisfy this control.

verification.method: Request each referenced image URL without cookies as a declared crawler user agent and record the status code alongside the matching crawl directive.

caution: Being fetchable is a precondition for appearing in image results. It does not cause an image to be included, and no control in this registry can promise inclusion.
